title: Pilot study on the prophylactic use of Cell Salvage in elective Cesarean Section without increased risk of Postpartum Hemorrhage
summary:
The automated processing of wound blood lost during an operation is routinely
used in many operations, including caesarean sections with high blood loss.
The return of processed blood is a safe, effective method of preventing and treating anaemia. In this study, wound blood from caesarean deliveries is to be collected in a specially in a specially approved device. The wound blood can be washed and processed as soon as 125 ml can be collected. In this case, the blood will be returned to the mothers via the vein. We suspect that this will prevent or mitigate the occurrence of anemia, resulting in improved health-related quality of life and resilience in the months following childbirth. This is to be determined using a standardized questionnaire to record health-related quality of life.

interventions.name: The study plans to recruit 20 patients scheduled for elective cesarean sections without increased risk of perioperative bleeding where intraoperative cell salvage will be utilized. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Capacity to consent, scheduled for elective cesarean Section
Exclusion criteria:
- Predictable risk factors for blood loss > 1000 ml, modified according to AWMF guideline 015/063:  
  - Previous uterine surgeries (especially cesarean section and transmural myomectomy)  
  - Placenta previa  
  - Multiple pregnancy  
  - Known coagulopathy  

- Suspected bacterial contamination of the surgical site or evidence thereof  
- Suspected bacteremia (e.g., sepsis)  

- Predictable risk factors for an allogeneic blood transfusion, modified according to AWMF guideline 015/063:  
  - Anemia (Hb < 9 g/dl) from 35 weeks of gestation onward
